import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Identify strongly associated features (p < 0.001)
    strong_features = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if abs(feats.x[:, i]).mean() > 0.1:  # Standardized values with substantial variation
            strong_features.append(fid)
    
    # Remove near-duplicates based on correlation
    correlated_pairs = set()
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(feats.ids):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(feats.ids[i+1:], i+1):
            corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, i], feats.x[:, j])[0, 1]
            if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                fid1_idx = feats.column(fid1)
                fid2_idx = feats.column(fid2)
                if fid1_idx < fid2_idx:
                    correlated_pairs.add((fid1, fid2))
                else:
                    correlated_pairs.add((fid2, fid1))
    
    # Build clusters of correlated features
    clusters = []
    used = set()
    for fid1, fid2 in sorted(correlated_pairs):
        if fid1 in used or fid2 in used:
            continue
        cluster = {fid1, fid2}
        used.add(fid1)
        used.add(fid2)
        # Extend cluster by adding more correlated features
        for fid3, fid4 in correlated_pairs:
            if fid3 in cluster or fid4 in cluster:
                cluster.add(fid3)
                cluster.add(fid4)
                used.add(fid3)
                used.add(fid4)
        clusters.append(list(cluster))
    
    # Select representative features from clusters
    representatives = []
    for cluster in clusters:
        # Prefer clinical over expression/copy_number if available
        clinical = [f for f in cluster if feats.types[feats.column(f)] == 'clinical']
        if clinical:
            representatives.extend(clinical)
        else:
            # Otherwise pick the one with highest absolute correlation strength
            best_fid = max(cluster, key=lambda f: abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, feats.column(f)], feats.y)[0, 1]))
            representatives.append(best_fid)
    
    # For non-clustered features, select those with highest effect size
    non_clustered = [f for f in strong_features if f not in representatives]
    # Sort by effect size (difference in means between outcome groups)
    def effect_size(fid):
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        y0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, idx]
        y1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, idx]
        return abs(y1.mean() - y0.mean())
    
    non_clustered.sort(key=effect_size, reverse=True)
    representatives.extend(non_clustered[:MAX_DRIVERS - len(representatives)])
    
    # Limit to maximum drivers
    representatives = representatives[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # Create products of top features
    products = []
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(representatives):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(representatives[i+1:], i+1):
            products.append((fid1, fid2))
    
    # Use all features with strong associations
    columns = representatives
    
    # Weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for fid in representatives:
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        effect = abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, idx], feats.y)[0, 1])
        loadings[fid] = effect
    
    # Drivers: strongest features that might be causal
    drivers = representatives[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=tuple(columns), products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
